images.caption: Figure 2:SpecWM overview.Top: decoded-frame reward verification and SpecWM’s latent verification with transition-aware refinement. Main: a fixed final-stage target probe supplies a score and a reusable clean prediction. Two thresholds select Accept, Refine, or Reject. One-step Refine reuses the prediction; longer corrections follow the3→2→13\to 2\to 1schedule near control transitions. Fig.3details overlapped execution and re-proposal. Right: selected quality and control scores, and speedups of Draft-only, Target-only, and SpecWM on WBench Navigation and LongSpecBench (Tables1and3), allowing direct comparison across both evaluation settings.

Figure 3:Overlapped speculative execution.Top: Draft-only and Target-only rollouts. Bottom: SpecWM drafts the next chunk while verifying the current one. Accept preserves the next proposal; committing a refined or regenerated chunk invalidates it. Dashed proposals are discarded and re-proposed after rollback, using the updated history that includes the committed output.

Figure 4:WBench quality-speed-control comparison.Top: Imaging versus NavScore; dotted arrows indicate increasing refinement length within each policy family. Bottom: generation-loop speedup over Target-only. Longer fixed refinements improve navigation but reduce speed. In comparison, SpecWM achieves the highest Imaging and NavScore at 1.63×\timesspeedup (Table1).

Figure 5:Qualitative comparison under changing controls.Target-only, Draft-only, SDVG-style, and SpecWM share the inputs and control sequence in each case. Control inputs are shown below the frames. Highlighted regions mark control failures and geometry collapse. SpecWM follows the changing controls while preserving scene structure across both sequences.
